substantive_analysis.title: Natural Capital and Sustainable Development
substantive_analysis.supplied_version: Journal article reproduced through JSTOR with one cover page
substantive_analysis.edition_relation: The article identity and printed span correspond to the syllabus; the PDF has 11 physical pages.
substantive_analysis.source_bound_claim: Costanza and Daly distinguish natural-capital stocks from service flows and propose limits on harvesting and waste emissions relative to regeneration and assimilative capacity.

argument_steps.label: Stock and flow
argument_steps.statement: Natural capital is a stock yielding future goods and services; reducing a demand flow does not by itself show maintenance of the supporting stock.

argument_steps.label: Ecological criterion
argument_steps.statement: Proposed harvesting and emission constraints refer to regeneration and assimilative capacities, rather than equipment performance alone.

argument_steps.label: Measurement limit
argument_steps.statement: The principles are not a complete operational measurement blueprint. A local application needs compatible abstraction, recharge and ecological observations.
argument_steps.locator_or_basis: Printed p.45; PDF p.10 plus study-specific dependency

substantive_analysis.permitted_use: Keep project demand, ecological stock and ecosystem-service claims separate.
substantive_analysis.prohibited_inference: Do not infer aquifer recovery or sustainability from a proposed flow-rate reduction.
qualifications: The operational principles fall short of a complete measurement blueprint; printed p. 45.
No local aquifer stock, recharge, abstraction or ecosystem observation is supplied.
substantive_analysis.missing_dependency: Human source-fidelity and assignment-fit review; original Cerrillos instruments for any case-specific claim
substantive_analysis.case_application_status: proposed analytical use; not a case finding
